scalesUsed.application: The iconic fuzz riff is built entirely from E major pentatonic, giving it its bright, singable quality

scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G# - A - B - C# - D - E
scalesUsed.application: The overall harmonic framework blending major tonality with the flattened 7th for a bluesy rock feel

mainProgression.description: The main riff is built on the simplest possible harmonic foundation - a two-chord I-IV alternation in E major, with the fuzz guitar providing all the melodic interest

sectionProgressions.description: The iconic fuzz riff plays over the I-IV vamp, creating one of the most recognizable guitar lines in history
Verse adds the B chord (V) for additional harmonic movement during vocal sections
Return to the two-chord riff foundation for the chorus, reinforcing the hook

harmonicFunction: E (I) - Tonic chord establishing the bright major key center
A (IV) - Subdominant providing the simple but effective harmonic movement
B (V) - Dominant chord adding direction in the verse sections
The I-IV vamp is one of the simplest yet most effective progressions in rock
The harmonic simplicity allows the fuzz riff melody to be the star of the show

techniques.name: Fuzz Tone Guitar Riff
techniques.description: THE riff - one of the most recognizable guitar lines in rock history. A simple two-note pattern played with heavy fuzz distortion, based on the E major pentatonic scale. Keith Richards famously dreamed this riff and recorded it on a cassette player in his sleep.

notes: The riff uses just the E and B strings in open position and 2nd-4th frets
Core pattern: 0-0-2-3-3-3-2-0 on the A and D strings
Based entirely on E major pentatonic scale tones
The fuzz tone is essential - the riff was written on a fuzz pedal
Play with confident, deliberate attack for the right feel
sequence: Start on the open A string (E note)
Play the ascending two-note motif (E to F# to G#)
Hit the held notes with sustain from the fuzz
Resolve back down to the open E/A notes
Repeat the pattern over the I-IV chord change
tips: The fuzz tone does a lot of the heavy lifting - get the tone right first
Keep the phrasing loose and confident rather than rigid
Use a medium-heavy pick for thick, defined fuzz notes
Mute unused strings carefully - fuzz amplifies any unwanted noise
This is a great first riff for beginners to learn
details.progression: Fuzz riff over E - A (I - IV)

techniques.name: Open Chord Rhythm Playing
techniques.description: Basic open chord strumming supporting the verse and chorus sections, using simple E, A, and B major chords with a driving rhythm feel

notes: E: 0-2-2-1-0-0 (Open E major chord)
A: X-0-2-2-2-0 (Open A major chord)
B: X-2-4-4-4-2 (B major barre chord) or B7: X-2-1-2-0-2 (easier alternative)
Simple downstroke strumming pattern on the rhythmic accents
Keep the strumming relaxed and groovy rather than stiff
sequence: Strum E major with confident downstrokes
Transition to A major on the chord change
During the verse, add the B chord for the V movement
Return to E-A for the chorus riff sections
tips: If B major barre chord is too difficult, use B7 as a substitute
Focus on the groove and feel rather than complex strumming patterns
Let the chords ring naturally without heavy palm muting
Match the energy of the fuzz riff when playing rhythm alongside it
details.progression: E - A - E - A (riff) / E - B - A (verse)

techniques.name: Two-Note Riff Pattern
techniques.description: The fundamental two-note melodic motif at the heart of the Satisfaction riff, teaching beginners how a simple interval can create an unforgettable hook

notes: The riff's core is built on seconds and thirds within the E major pentatonic scale
Two notes played in sequence with rhythmic emphasis creates the hook
The pattern repeats with slight variations over the chord changes
This technique demonstrates how simplicity creates memorability in rock guitar
sequence: Play the first note of the motif with strong pick attack
Follow with the second note, sustaining through the fuzz
Add the rhythmic pattern that gives the riff its swagger
Repeat and vary slightly over the E to A chord change
tips: Focus on the rhythmic placement of each note - timing is everything
The fuzz sustain helps notes connect smoothly
Practice the two-note motif in isolation before playing the full riff
Listen to how the riff interacts with the drum beat for the proper feel
details.progression: Two-note motif over E - A vamp

sections.name: Intro / Main Riff
sections.description: The song opens with one of the most iconic riffs in rock history - the fuzz-drenched two-note guitar line over the E-A vamp, immediately establishing the song's identity
notes: The fuzz riff stands alone at the start before the full band enters
Simple E major pentatonic-based melody with heavy fuzz distortion
Confident, rhythmic delivery is essential for the right feel
This riff was originally created by Keith Richards using a Maestro Fuzz-Tone pedal

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: The verse expands the harmony with the addition of the B chord, as rhythm guitar provides a driving bed for the vocal melody while the fuzz riff continues in the background
notes: Three-chord progression adds harmonic variety to the verse
Rhythm guitar strumming supports the vocal melody
Fuzz riff may continue subtly in the background
Keep the feel loose and groovy - not too rigid

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The chorus brings back the iconic fuzz riff front and center, with the full band driving the I-IV vamp underneath the vocal hook
notes: Return to the two-chord E-A foundation
Fuzz riff becomes the primary melodic element again
Full band energy at maximum for the chorus
The simplicity of the harmony keeps focus on the vocal and riff hooks

sections.name: Instrumental Break
sections.description: Extended instrumental section featuring the fuzz riff with the full band, allowing the guitar to take the spotlight with variations on the main riff theme
notes: The fuzz riff takes center stage without vocals
Slight variations and embellishments on the main riff pattern
Energy maintains at full level through the break
Demonstrates how the simple riff can carry an entire section

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: The song drives to its conclusion with the fuzz riff repeating over the E-A vamp, fading out as the band maintains the driving groove
notes: Continuous repetition of the main fuzz riff
Gradual fade-out on the original recording
Maintain full energy and consistent playing through the fade
The riff's persistence is what makes the ending memorable

guitar.recommended: Gibson Les Paul or Fender Telecaster
alternatives: Any electric guitar works - the fuzz pedal is more important than the guitar
guitar.pickup: Humbuckers or single coils both work - the fuzz pedal defines the tone

alternatives: Any clean amp that takes pedals well

settings.gain: 3/10 (clean - let the fuzz pedal handle the distortion)

effects.distortion: Maestro Fuzz-Tone (original) or any quality fuzz pedal (Electro-Harmonix Big Muff, Dunlop Fuzz Face, etc.)
effects.other: The fuzz pedal is the essential effect - everything else is optional

beginner.title: Learning the Iconic Riff
steps: Learn the open E and A major chord shapes
Practice the basic fuzz riff melody at slow tempo (70-80 BPM)
Work on clean transitions between E and A chords
Add the fuzz effect and practice the riff with the proper tone

intermediate.title: Full Song Structure and Rhythm
steps: Learn the verse progression with the B chord
Master the full song structure including all section transitions
Practice the driving strumming rhythm at increasing speeds
Build tempo from 90 BPM to the full 136 BPM

advanced.title: Performance Polish and Tone Matching
steps: Play the complete song at full tempo with authentic tone
Add dynamic variation between verse and chorus sections
Develop improvisational variations on the main riff
Match the loose, confident feel of the original Keith Richards performance

commonMistakes: Playing the riff too precisely and stiffly - it should have a loose, swagger feel
Not using a fuzz pedal - the tone is absolutely essential to the riff's character
Unwanted string noise from the fuzz amplifying buzzes and overtones
Rushing the riff tempo instead of locking into the groove at 136 BPM
Overcomplicating the riff - the beauty is in its simplicity
practiceRoutine: Learn the two-note riff motif on a clean tone first for 5 minutes
Add the fuzz effect and practice muting unused strings cleanly
Work on the E-A chord change timing with the riff overlay
Practice the verse chord progression (E-B-A) at slow tempo
Play the full song along with the original recording
focusAreas: Clean fuzz tone without unwanted string noise or feedback
Rhythmic confidence and swagger in the riff delivery
Smooth E to A transitions maintaining the riff flow
Groove and feel - this riff is about attitude more than precision
String muting technique to control fuzz pedal noise
metronomeWork: Practice the riff at 70 BPM to nail the note placement precisely
Increase by 10 BPM per session once the notes are clean
At 100 BPM, add the chord changes underneath the riff
Practice the verse E-B-A progression at 110 BPM before building speed
Target tempo is 136 BPM - focus on locking into the groove
